findings.violating_statement: The administrative particulars provide only the Basic UDI‑DI codes for the devices and do not include the required UDI‑PI (e.g., lot or serial number) for implantable devices as required by the MDR.
findings.source_quote: Basic UDI-DI Codes: Double J Stent & Kit Blue (Short Term); 890551639TL. Basic UDI-DI Codes: Blue HC; 8905516101AW. Basic UDI-DI Codes: Blue Set; 890551640T5. Basic UDI-DI Codes: Blue Set HC; 8905516100AV. Basic UDI-DI Codes: Double J Stent & Kit White (Short Term); 890551641T7. Basic UDI-DI Codes: White HC; 8905516107BA. Basic UDI-DI Codes: White Set; 890551642T9. Basic UDI-DI Codes: White Set HC; 8905516108BC.
findings.explanation: Annex VI.C.6.b mandates that implantable devices must have the UDI‑PI (lot or serial number) identifiable prior to implantation. The CER section lists only the UDI‑DI values and omits any UDI‑PI information, which means the requirement is not met.
findings.suggested_correction: Add the corresponding UDI‑PI (lot/serial number) for each listed implantable device, e.g., "Basic UDI‑DI Code: ...; UDI‑PI (Lot/Serial): XYZ123" for each entry.

findings.violating_statement: The device description does not provide the full identification and description required by Annex XV 2.1, such as risk classification, design and manufacturing details, and reference to previous generations.
findings.source_quote: Double J Stent is used for treatment of the upper urinary tract are implantable devices that support the flow of the urine from the kidneys to the bladder.
findings.explanation: Annex XV 2.1 mandates a comprehensive identification and description of the device, including intended purpose, risk classification, design, manufacturing information and reference to prior generations. The CER section only gives a brief functional description and omits these required details, constituting non‑compliance.
findings.suggested_correction: Include a detailed device description covering: intended purpose, risk class and classification rule, design and manufacturing processes, materials used, and reference to any previous or similar device generations, as required by Annex XV 2.1.

findings.violating_statement: The biocompatibility information is limited to a summary of ISO 10993 tests without detailed test design, protocols, data analysis or rationale, which is required by Annex II.6.b.
findings.source_quote: Biocompatibility; Specifications: Evaluated in accordance with ISO 10993 series; passed Cytotoxicity, Intracutaneous Reactivity, and Skin Sensitization testing.
findings.explanation: Annex II.6.b mandates detailed information on test design, methods of data analysis and test conclusions for biocompatibility, including identification of all materials in contact. The CER only provides a brief statement of test outcomes, lacking the required depth.
findings.suggested_correction: Include a detailed biocompatibility section describing the test protocols, sample preparation, data analysis methods, results summaries for each ISO 10993 test, and justification for any reliance on previous data.

findings.violating_statement: The packaging description does not demonstrate that the device will remain sterile until use, nor does it provide evidence of validated sterile packaging integrity as required by Annex I.11.d.
findings.source_quote: Packaging; Specifications: Primary: Polyurethane cover with Tyvek pouch Secondary: Duplex box Tertiary: 5-ply corrugated box.
findings.explanation: Annex I.11.d requires that devices delivered in a sterile state be packaged in a way that ensures sterility is maintained until the package is opened, with validated methods and clear evidence of packaging integrity. The CER only lists packaging components without any validation or integrity evidence.
findings.suggested_correction: Add documentation of validated sterile packaging processes, sterility assurance level (SAL) data, and a description of how the integrity of the Tyvek pouch and outer boxes is verified throughout transport and storage.

findings.violating_statement: The report does not provide a statement confirming the compatibility between the different parts of the device as required by Annex I > (10) > (c).
findings.source_quote: The combination of polyurethane for the stent body and polypropylene-based accessory components ensures flexibility, mechanical strength, chemical resistance, and compatibility with Ethylene Oxide (EtO) sterilization, thereby supporting the safety and performance of the Double J Stent (Short Term) for its intended use.
findings.explanation: Annex I 10 c requires explicit confirmation that the different parts of a multi‑part device are compatible with each other. The CER only mentions overall material suitability and sterilisation compatibility, but does not address part‑to‑part compatibility (e.g., chemical interaction between polyurethane and polypropylene).
findings.suggested_correction: Add a statement such as: "Compatibility testing between the polyurethane stent body and all polypropylene components (pusher, string, sheath, clamp) has been performed in accordance with Annex I 10 c and demonstrated no adverse chemical or mechanical interactions under intended use conditions."

findings.violating_statement: The report lacks a confirmation that the device meets defined chemical and/or physical specifications as required by Annex I > (10) > (h).
findings.source_quote: The materials selected for device construction are widely used in urological medical devices and are suitable for short-term internal use.
findings.explanation: Annex I 10 h mandates that the device meets defined chemical and physical specifications and that such specifications are documented. The CER only states that materials are "widely used" and "suitable" without providing the specific chemical/physical limits or test results.
findings.suggested_correction: Include detailed chemical and physical specifications (e.g., tensile strength, elongation, leachable limits) for each material and reference the test data confirming compliance with those specifications.

findings.violating_statement: The report does not provide evidence of compatibility between the different parts of the device (e.g., pusher, guidewire, stent) as required by Annex I 10 c.
findings.source_quote: Pusher (introducer sheath) with/without Radiopaque pusher and guidewire connected as a unit which allows for manipulation or push the stents to accurate position over a compatible guidewire (all category)
findings.explanation: Annex I 10 c mandates that the compatibility between the different parts of a device consisting of more than one implantable part be demonstrated. The CER section merely lists the parts without any compatibility assessment or testing data, constituting a breach.
findings.suggested_correction: Include a statement and supporting data that demonstrate the mechanical and functional compatibility of the pusher, guidewire, and Double J stent (e.g., results of bench testing, material compatibility studies).

findings.violating_statement: The report lacks confirmation that the device meets defined chemical and physical specifications, as required by Annex I 10 h.
findings.explanation: Annex I 10 h requires confirmation that the device meets defined chemical and/or physical specifications and that design minimizes risks from contaminants and residues. The CER only mentions material composition without providing the required specifications or verification data.
findings.suggested_correction: Add detailed chemical and physical specifications for all materials (e.g., grade, surface finish, corrosion resistance) and describe verification activities confirming compliance.

raw.violating_statement: The description of the mechanism of action lacks any scientific evidence or data to demonstrate the principles of operation and mode of action as required by Annex.II.1.d.
raw.source_quote: The mechanism of action is mechanical and is based on the following: 1. Internal Urinary Drainage ... 5. Temporary Support Function The device is intended for short-term use (up to 30 days) and provides temporary mechanical support to ensure drainage until the underlying condition is resolved or further intervention is performed.
raw.explanation: Annex.II.1.d mandates that the principles of operation and mode of action be scientifically demonstrated where necessary. The CER section only narrates the functional description without presenting any scientific data, studies, or references to substantiate the claimed mechanical action.
raw.suggested_correction: Include references to pre‑clinical or clinical studies that quantitatively demonstrate the mechanical drainage performance of the Double J Stent, such as flow rate measurements, patency rates, or comparative data with equivalent devices, thereby providing the required scientific justification for the described principles of operation.

findings.violating_statement: The report does not specify the sterilisation method for the sterile device as required
findings.source_quote: This is a single use sterile device which is used for internal drainage from Kidney to Bladder in medical conditions like improper urine drainage, calculi in ureter, hydronephrosis, oxalate calculi, pyeloplasty with UPJ Obstruction, residual renal calculus, ureteral stricture.
findings.explanation: Annex I.23.l requires that if the device is supplied sterile, the CER must indicate the sterilisation method. The provided section only states the device is sterile but gives no method details, breaching the clause.
findings.suggested_correction: Add a statement such as: "The device is supplied sterile, sterilised by ethylene oxide (EO) according to validated process XYZ, with accompanying validation reports."

findings.violating_statement: Missing indication of the sterilisation method for the sterile device
findings.source_quote: This is a single use sterile device used for internal drainage from Kidney to Bladder
findings.explanation: Clause (l) requires that when a device is supplied sterile, the CER must indicate the sterile state and the sterilisation method. The statement only declares the device is sterile but does not specify the sterilisation method, breaching the clause.
findings.suggested_correction: This is a single‑use sterile device, sterilised by ethylene‑oxide, used for internal drainage from kidney to bladder

findings.violating_statement: Missing indication that the product is a medical device
findings.source_quote: This is a single use sterile device used for internal drainage from Kidney to Bladder
findings.explanation: Clause (q) mandates an explicit indication that the product is a medical device. The current description does not contain such an indication, resulting in non‑compliance.
findings.suggested_correction: This is a single‑use sterile medical device used for internal drainage from kidney to bladder

findings.violating_statement: The intended patient population description lacks required patient selection criteria, contraindications and warnings
findings.source_quote: Double J Stent (Short term) is manufactured to meet requirements of medical conditions like Improper urine drainage, calculi in ureter, hydronephrosis, oxalate calculi, pyeloplasty with UPJ Obstruction, residual renal calculus, ureteral stricture. These medical conditions commonly occur in adult Male, Female during urological procedures. Hence Double J Stent (Short term) can be use in Adults, Male / Female.
findings.explanation: Annex.II.1.c requires the intended patient population to include patient selection criteria, indications, contra‑indications and warnings. The CER section only lists conditions and a generic adult population, omitting any contraindications, warnings or detailed selection criteria, thus not meeting the clause.
findings.suggested_correction: Include a detailed description of patient selection criteria, specific indications, any known contraindications, and relevant warnings for the Double J Stent (Short term) in the intended patient population section.

findings.violating_statement: The report does not provide the required technical, biological and clinical equivalence justification for using data from similar generic devices, as required by Annex XIV.A.3.
findings.source_quote: The Double J Stent/Kit (Long Term) is a first-generation device. However, similar generic devices have been on the market for some time and have well-established technology (WET)
findings.explanation: Annex XIV.A.3 mandates that a clinical evaluation based on equivalence must detail technical, biological and clinical characteristics showing no clinically significant differences. The CER section only states that similar devices exist and have well‑established technology, without describing design, materials, usage conditions, or clinical performance comparability.
findings.suggested_correction: Include a detailed equivalence analysis covering: (i) technical similarity (design, specifications, deployment method), (ii) biological similarity (materials, contact duration, release characteristics), and (iii) clinical similarity (indications, patient population, performance outcomes) with scientific justification that no clinically significant differences exist.

raw.violating_statement: The report states that no clinical investigation was performed based solely on MDR article 61, without demonstrating that an exemption under Art.61.4 applies.
raw.source_quote: Hence, according to MDR article 61, no clinical investigation was performed.
raw.explanation: Art.61.4 requires a clinical investigation for implantable devices unless specific exemption criteria are met (e.g., equivalence demonstrated and endorsed by the notified body). The CER does not provide evidence that any of these exemption conditions are satisfied, making the claim non‑compliant.
raw.suggested_correction: Provide evidence that the device meets one of the exemption criteria of Art.61.4 (e.g., documented equivalence assessment endorsed by the notified body) or conduct and report a clinical investigation as required.

findings.violating_statement: The report does not describe a proactive and systematic process to collect post‑market information, nor does it specify indicators, thresholds or methods to assess the collected data as required by the post‑market surveillance plan.
findings.source_quote: The device is marketed in India. The following data sources were utilised to collect relevant post‑marketing data to support clinical safety and performance.
findings.explanation: Annex III.b mandates that the PMS plan must cover a proactive systematic collection process, suitable indicators and methods to assess data. The CER only lists data sources without describing the systematic process, indicators or assessment methods, thus breaching the clause.
findings.suggested_correction: Include a description of the systematic PMS process, define specific performance indicators and threshold values, and detail the methods and tools used to assess and analyse the collected post‑market data.

findings.violating_statement: No periodic safety update report (PSUR) is mentioned, contrary to the requirement for class IIa/IIb/III devices.
findings.source_quote: A total number of 250 patients were treated during this process. However, 8 incidents of complications related to the application of the device was reported by those professionals:
findings.explanation: Article 86.1 requires manufacturers to prepare a PSUR summarising PMS data and corrective actions. The CER excerpt provides incident numbers but does not reference a PSUR or its contents, indicating a missing requirement.
findings.suggested_correction: Add a section summarising the PSUR, including analysis of the reported incidents, conclusions, and any preventive or corrective actions taken.

raw.violating_statement: The clinical evaluation documentation is not shown to be updated with post‑market data throughout the device life‑cycle as required.
raw.source_quote: The device is marketed in India. The following data sources were utilised to collect relevant post‑marketing data to support clinical safety and performance.
raw.explanation: Article 61.11 obliges continuous updating of the clinical evaluation with data from the PMCF plan and PMS plan. The CER only lists data sources without indicating that the clinical evaluation has been updated accordingly.
raw.suggested_correction: State explicitly that the clinical evaluation report has been updated with the presented post‑market data, referencing the relevant sections and dates of update.
